skill.name: tests-maintenance
skill.description: Maintains IdeaVim test quality by reviewing disabled tests, documenting Neovim exclusions, improving readability, and keeping each change focused.
skill.summary: Review and improve one focused area of the IdeaVim test suite.
skill.author: JetBrains

security_audit.summary: All 76 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documented local test commands, or ordinary review wording. The skill contains no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, covert network access, or unsafe command construction.

content.user_title: Maintain IdeaVim Tests with Focused Reviews
content.value_statement: Disabled tests and unclear exclusions can hide regressions and weaken test quality. This skill reviews one focused area and produces documented, reviewable maintenance changes.
actual_capabilities: Selects one IdeaVim test file or method for a focused maintenance run.
Finds disabled Kotlin tests and checks whether targeted Gradle tests now pass.
Reviews TestWithoutNeovim reasons and requires descriptions for non-obvious exclusions.
Runs targeted or standard Gradle tests, including optional Neovim verification.
Replaces meaningless test content with realistic examples and improves test names.
Prepares a focused pull request title and body describing the review and changes.
limitations: The workflow is tailored to the IdeaVim repository structure, annotations, and Gradle tasks.
Test execution requires the repository dependencies and any configured Neovim test environment.
The skill does not fix production bugs, implement features, or perform major refactoring.
Passing tests do not prove that an exclusion is obsolete without reviewing history and behavior.

use_cases.title: Recheck Disabled Tests
use_cases.description: Run one disabled test, investigate its history, and re-enable it only when the result is stable and explained.

use_cases.title: Document Neovim Exclusions
use_cases.description: Replace vague exclusion reasons with specific categories and descriptions supported by test results or repository evidence.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Readability
use_cases.description: Replace meaningless fixture text and clarify test names while preserving the tested behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Disabled Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Find one disabled IdeaVim test, run it, and report whether it can be re-enabled. Explain the evidence and keep changes limited to that test.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Neovim Exclusion
prompt_templates.prompt: Review one TestWithoutNeovim annotation. Verify the reason, run the test with Neovim when possible, and add a specific description if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Improve One Test File
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect one IdeaVim test file for unclear names or meaningless content. Make one logical readability improvement without changing production behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Deprecated Exclusions
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose one DIFFERENT or UNCLEAR exclusion. Test with Neovim, inspect relevant history, classify the cause, and prepare a focused pull request summary.

output_examples.output: Reviewed DeleteMotionTest. The targeted test passed consistently after the referenced fix, so the disabled annotation was removed with a focused explanation.
The exclusion reflects an IntelliJ editor offset difference. The reason was updated and a description now explains the observed behavior.

output_examples.input: Improve readability in one test file.
output_examples.output: Replaced meaningless fixture text with a realistic Kotlin example. Assertions and production code were unchanged.

best_practices: Keep each run and pull request limited to one logical test maintenance change.
Verify Neovim mode is active before drawing conclusions from compatibility test results.
Use test output, history, comments, or platform documentation to justify exclusion reasons.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated annotation, content, and disabled-test changes in one pull request.
Do not classify intentional behavior differences from assumptions without supporting evidence.
Do not expand maintenance work into production fixes, new features, or major refactoring.

faq.question: Can this skill re-enable disabled tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It runs a targeted test and requires investigation before removing the disabled annotation.

faq.question: Does it support Neovim compatibility checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run configured Gradle tests with Neovim verification and checks that Neovim testing is active.

faq.question: Will it fix production code?
faq.answer: No. Its scope is test maintenance, documentation, and readability.

faq.question: How many tests does one run change?
faq.answer: Usually one test file or method. Identical annotation fixes may be grouped when they represent one logical issue.

faq.question: What evidence supports an exclusion reason?
faq.answer: Useful evidence includes test output, commit history, code comments, platform documentation, and clear platform constraints.

faq.question: What happens when no change is needed?
faq.answer: The skill reports what it checked and explains that no maintenance change was necessary.
